headline: Highest risk is medium: shared browser-based workflows can leak or misroute content, while prompt-injection and capability-conflict are limited by the pair’s mostly separate execution surfaces.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Agent A can ingest browser/file content and runtime-injected MCPs/hooks; Agent B runs browsers and processes uploaded documents, but B has no filesystem write or MCP use. The pair lacks a direct shared channel by default, so injection is possible mainly through manual copy/paste or content passed through browser workflows, not a strong default bridge.
conditions: IF operator copies A-generated content into B prompts or uploads A-produced files into B
IF A's browser output is treated as instructions by B without provenance checks
mitigations: Disable copy-paste of untrusted web text into either agent
Require provenance labels on any A output before B consumes it
Use a separate workspace for browser-derived artifacts
Turn off runtime-injected MCPs/hooks for untrusted tasks
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and instruction-stripping before handoff

B_data_leakage.rationale: A touches provider auth data, session history, project code, and AGENTS.md/README.md, while B uploads documents and browsing context to a vendor-hosted service. Even without a shared filesystem, leakage can occur if A forwards sensitive local context into B's prompts or uploads, and B's vendor-only egress makes that exposure external by default.
conditions: IF A includes provider auth data or session history in prompts sent to B
IF A uploads project files or AGENTS.md content into B's document analysis
IF B retains uploaded documents or browsing context beyond the intended task
mitigations: Redact secrets before any A-to-B transfer
Keep auth prompts out of B inputs
Use separate accounts for A and B
Upload only minimal excerpts to B
requires-engineering: enforce DLP on handoff content

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A can spawn subprocesses and has broad network egress, while B cannot write the filesystem, execute shell, install packages, or modify git state. Their mutable-resource overlap is therefore limited; the main conflict is concurrent browser/network activity rather than direct write contention, so the blast radius is small.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same external web service or API quota
IF A's subprocesses and B's browser sessions compete for the same user account state
mitigations: Stagger browser-heavy tasks
Use separate accounts or API keys
Avoid concurrent runs against the same web app
Pause A while B is performing searches
requires-engineering: add orchestration locks for shared external resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: A can produce project code, README/AGENTS.md-derived context, and browser-sourced outputs; B is a search-RAG answer engine that can render or summarize inputs. If A's output is handed to B as authoritative, B may amplify errors into polished answers, but B's search/citation workflow provides some verification, so this is not high.
conditions: IF B is prompted to trust A's output without independent search or citation checks
IF A's generated code or facts are reused by B in a final answer
mitigations: Require B to cite independent sources
Mark A output as untrusted draft text
Compare A claims against live search before reuse
Limit A-to-B handoffs to summaries only
requires-engineering: add verification gates between agents

E_compliance.rationale: A handles provider auth prompts and installation identifiers; B handles uploaded documents and browsing context under a vendor-hosted privacy policy. The profiles do not show a specific residency or regulated-data mismatch, so compliance risk is limited to policy mismatch if sensitive data is routed from A into B.
conditions: IF regulated data from A is uploaded into B
IF B's retention policy differs from the operator's required retention for A's data classes
mitigations: Do not send secrets to B
Review B's retention settings before upload
Use non-sensitive test data
Separate regulated and non-regulated workflows
requires-engineering: implement data-class routing rules
